phases.raw:
{
"modality": "cli_tool",
"rationale": "A headless CLI utility is the most efficient way to integrate into a CI pipeline, allowing for the transient deployment of an echo server and the generation of machine-readable logs for automated verification.",
"constraints": [
"Implement structured JSON logging for seamless CI log parsing",
"HTTP echo server must be lightweight with minimal memory overhead",
"Must be compatible with existing .\scripts\run-smoke-ci.ps1 execution flow",
"No external runtime dependencies to ensure rapid container/VM boot times",
"Include configurable timeouts and port assignments to avoid CI environment collisions"
],
"ceo_summary": "We are hardening our deployment pipeline by introducing deterministic network verification to eliminate false positives in our smoke tests.",
"cpo_summary": "The tool will provide a lean, observable endpoint to validate connectivity and payload integrity during the CI phase."
}

parsed.build_notes: Integrate via CMake as a standalone utility target; leverage existing build.bat for MSVC environment; ensure structured logs output to stdout/file for CI parsing.
parsed.cto_summary: Implementing a lightweight C++20 headless echo server to extend CI smoke coverage with high-performance, structured verification.
risks: Port availability in headless CI environments
Dependency bloat for a minimal echo server
